paper.title_en: A higher-order smoothness indicator as refinement criterion for Newtonian and relativistic MHD simulations
paper.abstract_en: Adaptive mesh refinement is a widely adopted strategy for grid-based numerical simulation codes to mitigate the high computational cost of multi-length scale problems. A robust and reliable mesh refinement criterion with minimal requirement for problem-specific tuning is critical for efficient and accurate simulations. Motivated by the oscillation indicators used in the spectral methods literature, we develop a new mesh refinement criterion employing a 5-point stencil for multi-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics simulations, essentially extending the conventional 3-point Löhner scheme. We implement the criterion in the astrophysical fluid dynamics code AthenaK and test it across a variety of benchmark problems in Newtonian, special relativistic, and general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, demonstrating its robustness and versatility.
